title: git-bundle-verify
capability_statement: Verify that a git bundle file is the artifact it claims to be: its SHA-256 matches the digest recorded for it, it records a complete history, it clones, and the tree it produces matches a reference checkout byte for byte. The package carries the defective bundles it must refuse, so the refusals are checkable by whoever adopted it.

scope.problem_class: Acceptance of a git bundle received as a release artifact: digest, completeness, cloneability and equality with a reference tree, decided offline and reproducibly.
non_goals: Fetching the bundle, or any other network access
Writing to the bundle, the reference tree, or any path outside the work directory
Judging the CONTENT of the history (review, licensing, provenance of individual commits)
Establishing PROVENANCE: the digest check proves the file is the one you were told about, not that the one who told you is to be trusted
Repairing or rewriting a bundle that fails a check
prerequisites: git 2.30 or newer on PATH — the runbook is about the behaviour of `git bundle verify`, so the lower bound is declared rather than assumed, and step 1 checks it

GNU coreutils on PATH (sha256sum, sort, cat, printf) and GNU sed — the scripts use spellings that exist only there: sha256sum as a program name, sort --version-sort, sed --quiet --expression. runtime.os is linux alone for exactly this reason, and it is a declaration rather than a preference: on a BSD userland these are different programs, and a script that chose between them would need a conditional, which gate 5 refuses
awk on PATH — any POSIX awk. It counts lines where `wc -l` would: `wc` pads its count to a column on some implementations, and g3 and g4 are declared as exact lines
read access to the bundle file and, for step 4, to the reference directory
a work directory that does not exist or is empty; step 1 refuses anything else, and the operator may delete it afterwards
the expected SHA-256 and the reference tree obtained by a DIFFERENT channel than the bundle itself

steps.instruction: Confirm the work directory, the git version and the bundle's digest. Run scripts/01-checksum.sh with three arguments: the bundle path, the expected SHA-256 as 64 lowercase hex characters, and the work directory. The script refuses a work directory that has anything in it (a populated one lets a failed run read an earlier run's artifacts as its own), refuses a git older than the declared minimum, MEASURES the bundle into actual.sha256, writes the digest you asserted into expected.sha256, and only then hands the latter to sha256sum in check mode, so a wrong digest ends the run before anything is cloned. Measuring before checking is what makes the refusal readable: the check is silent by contract, so both numbers being on disk is the whole of the diagnosis. On success the step also writes checksum-ok.txt, which is what step 2 refuses to run without — actual.sha256 exists after a refusal too and cannot stand for a passing check — and bundle-id.sha256, the BINDING: the digest it MEASURED, alone on its line with no path beside it. A token says a step agreed; it does not say about what, and BUNDLE_PATH is an argument the later steps are given again. Steps 2 and 3 compare their own input against this binding, so the chain is about one artifact rather than about a sequence of agreements. The digest is what is compared and the path is not, because the path is exactly what a substitution re-points. What this step establishes is exactly one thing: the file matches the digest you were given. It does not classify HOW a mismatching file differs. Substitute the three placeholder words with real paths and the real digest, which must have reached you by a different channel than the bundle.

Confirm the bundle carries a whole history rather than an increment. Run scripts/02-history.sh with the bundle path and the work directory. Its FIRST action is to remove history-ok.txt, its own PASS token from any earlier run in this work directory: a token is a claim about the run that wrote it, and it was outliving that run — a passing step 2 followed by a refusing one left the first run's token for step 3 to read and clone on. It then requires step 1's token, and then requires that the bundle in front of it be the one step 1 accepted: it measures its own BUNDLE_PATH, keeps the digest field alone, and compares it against bundle-id.sha256, before git init, before the header is read and before git bundle verify — so a switched bundle leaves no probe/, no prerequisites.txt and no bundle-verify.txt. Past those it creates an empty probe repository, because git refuses to verify a bundle outside a repository; extracts the bundle header's prerequisite lines into prerequisites.txt BEFORE verifying, so the classifier survives a refusal; and then requires two signals to agree — a zero exit status from git bundle verify, and an empty prerequisite list. The exit status is the refusal condition; the list is the cause, which the status alone cannot name. Past both signals the step writes history-ok.txt, which is what step 3 refuses to run without. bundle-verify.txt is NOT that token and never could be: it is created by the redirect that captures git's output, before that command has an exit status, so it survives a refusal — it holds the diagnosis, not the verdict. Because the token is destroyed at the top of every run of this step, a refusal at ANY of its signals leaves the chain with no usable token — neither this run's nor the previous run's — whichever bundle step 3 is then handed.

Clone the bundle into a disposable directory and report what it produced. Run scripts/03-clone.sh with the bundle path and the work directory. It refuses to run unless step 2 left history-ok.txt behind — the token only a PASSING step 2 writes, and only the LAST step 2 in this work directory can have left — so nothing is cloned after a refused completeness check; run out of order it names the missing artifact instead of letting git complain about prerequisite commits the operator never named. It then requires, as step 2 does and by the same three lines, that its own BUNDLE_PATH measure equal to bundle-id.sha256, BEFORE git clone: handed a valid, complete bundle of a DIFFERENT repository after a passing step 1 and step 2, this step used to clone it and report head-commit, head-tree, tracked-files and clone-ok over it, leaving the substitution to be noticed at step 4 by a tree that happened to differ. A refusal here creates no clone directory at all. It then prints the HEAD commit id, the HEAD tree id and the number of tracked files, then a completion token. Record all four lines: the three identity lines are the finding, and they are what a second reader compares against. This step, not step 2, is what catches a damaged or truncated packfile, because git bundle verify reads only the header.
steps.expected:
head-commit <40 hex>
head-tree <40 hex>
tracked-files <count>
clone-ok

steps.instruction: Compare the clone with the reference tree, file by file. Run scripts/04-compare.sh with the work directory and the reference directory. It refuses to run unless step 3 left its finding behind, then points the clone's own git directory at the reference tree as a work tree, so every tracked path is compared by content and nothing is written outside the work directory. The number printed is the count of tracked paths whose bytes differ; zero means the reference tree and the bundle agree exactly. The count is printed first and the refusal follows it, so the number is on stdout either way AND a non-zero count ends the run with a non-zero exit status: a caller that reads only exit statuses is refused too, and one that reads the number still gets it.

Self-check, before trusting a verdict from the four steps above: prove on this package that the runbook can REFUSE. The directory vectors/ carries four classes of defective bundle plus a positive control, and vectors/MATRIX.tsv gives, for each, the digest to pass to step 1, the step that must refuse it, and the evidence to look for. Run every row of the matrix, each in its own fresh work directory, and follow the reading in SKILL.md under Self-check. The positive control must be accepted and end in divergences 0; without it, a runbook that refused everything would look perfect. Then run the three sequence cases in SKILL.md under 'Self-check, part two', which use the same vectors and no others: A switches the bundle between step 1 and step 2, B switches it between step 2 and step 3, C runs a second step 2 that refuses and then offers step 3 the bundle the FIRST step 2 had passed. A row of MATRIX.tsv is one bundle walked in order and cannot express any of the three; they are kept out of the table rather than bent into it.
steps.expected: good.bundle accepted with divergences 0; corrupt and truncated refused at step 1 with the announced digest and at step 3 with their own; incremental refused at step 2 with a non-empty prerequisites.txt; foreign refused at step 4 with divergences 1 on stdout and a non-zero exit status. Sequence case A: step 2 exits non-zero with empty stdout, stderr names bundle-id.sha256, and the work directory holds no probe/, prerequisites.txt, bundle-verify.txt or history-ok.txt. Case B: step 3 exits non-zero with empty stdout, stderr names bundle-id.sha256, and no clone/ is created. Case C: the second step 2 refuses, and step 3 then refuses on history-ok.txt for BOTH incremental.bundle and good.bundle, cloning neither

expected_outputs: head-commit, head-tree and tracked-files, then clone-ok
every row of vectors/MATRIX.tsv refused at the step it names, and the positive control accepted

validation_gates.check: the work directory does not exist, or exists and is empty
validation_gates.pass_criteria: step 1's rmdir succeeds and the directory is created again; a populated directory survives rmdir, which fails with "Directory not empty" and ends the run with empty stdout

validation_gates.check: git is at least the declared minimum, 2.30.0
validation_gates.pass_criteria: sort --check --version-sort accepts the pair [required, actual]; an older git makes it report "disorder" on line 2 and ends the run

validation_gates.check: the bundle file's SHA-256 equals the digest passed on the command line
validation_gates.pass_criteria: stdout of step 1 == "bundle-sha256-ok"; any other digest makes sha256sum --check exit non-zero and set -e ends the run with empty stdout and empty stderr, which is the contract of --status and not an omission. The bundle is measured into actual.sha256 BEFORE the check, so a refusal leaves expected.sha256 and actual.sha256 side by side in the work directory and the mismatch is checkable there. Passing also writes checksum-ok.txt and bundle-id.sha256; a refusal leaves neither, and the printed line is unchanged — the digest stays out of stdout and out of the token, so an adopter matching the exact line matches the same line as before. What passing proves is exactly this and no more: the file matches the digest passed on the command line. It says nothing about who named that digest, and nothing about WHY a mismatching file differs — a flipped byte and a truncation are one event to a digest comparison, and the two are told apart at step 3

validation_gates.check: the BUNDLE_PATH given to step 2 and to step 3 is the same artifact step 1 accepted
validation_gates.pass_criteria: each of steps 2 and 3 measures its own BUNDLE_PATH, keeps the digest field alone, and cmp agrees with bundle-id.sha256 — the digest step 1 MEASURED past its own check. A mismatch, or a binding that is absent because step 1 refused or never ran, ends the step with a non-zero exit status and empty stdout, and stderr names the binding: cmp's difference report is redirected to stderr so the empty-stdout contract of a refusal holds. The comparison runs before either step touches the bundle for any other purpose, so a switched input leaves no probe/, no prerequisites.txt, no bundle-verify.txt and no clone/. The reading and not the path is what is compared: BUNDLE_PATH is the operator's argument and is exactly what a substitution re-points

validation_gates.check: git bundle verify accepts the bundle AND the bundle declares no prerequisites
validation_gates.pass_criteria: stdout of step 2 == "bundle-history-complete", which needs g1-binding to have agreed and then both signals: a zero exit status from git bundle verify (the refusal condition — non-zero for an increment, a damaged header or a file that is not a bundle, and unlike the sentence "The bundle records a complete history" neither localizable nor version-dependent), and an empty prerequisites.txt (the classifier that separates "incomplete history" from "not a bundle"). Passing also writes history-ok.txt, carrying the same bytes stdout got; a refusal at any signal leaves it absent while bundle-verify.txt and prerequisites.txt remain as evidence. Absent means absent for this work directory and not merely unwritten by this run: the token is removed as the step's first action, so an earlier run's cannot stand in for it

validation_gates.check: the bundle clones, and the clone's HEAD commit, HEAD tree and tracked-file count are reported
validation_gates.pass_criteria: stdout of step 3 ends with "clone-ok" and its first three lines read "head-commit <sha>", "head-tree <sha>", "tracked-files <n>". The step is guarded on history-ok.txt, so it does not run at all after a refused step 2 — no clone directory is created, stdout is empty, and stderr names the missing token — and on g1-binding, so it does not run on a bundle its two predecessors never saw either. The two guards answer different questions: the token says the last step 2 agreed, the binding says it agreed about this file

validation_gates.check: every tracked path in the reference tree is byte-identical to the same path in the clone
validation_gates.pass_criteria: stdout of step 4 == "divergences 0" AND step 4 exits 0. The two agree by construction: the count is printed, then compared against an empty file, so a non-zero count exits non-zero. Neither reading of the step can accept a divergent tree

validation_gates.check: the runbook refuses each defective bundle shipped in vectors/, at the step vectors/MATRIX.tsv names, and accepts the positive control
validation_gates.pass_criteria: all seven rows of vectors/MATRIX.tsv behave as recorded: refusals print nothing on stdout and stop, the incremental vector leaves a non-empty prerequisites.txt, the foreign vector reaches step 4, prints a non-zero count AND exits non-zero, and good.bundle ends in "divergences 0"

rollback: Delete the work directory. The runbook writes nowhere else: the bundle and the reference tree are opened read-only, and every git invocation is pointed at a git directory inside the work directory.
No registry, remote or system state is touched, so there is nothing else to undo.

failure_modes.symptom: step 1 prints nothing and exits non-zero; stderr reads "rmdir: failed to remove ...: Directory not empty"
failure_modes.mitigation: point the run at a fresh work directory; the runbook never deletes anything. Reusing a populated one is how a previous run's head-commit.txt or empty divergences.txt gets read as this run's result

failure_modes.symptom: step 1 prints nothing; stderr reads "sort: .../git-version-check.txt:2: disorder: git version <yours>"
failure_modes.mitigation: install git 2.30 or newer; the runbook uses no newer feature, and only the lower bound matters

failure_modes.symptom: step 1 exits non-zero with empty stdout AND empty stderr — sha256sum --status is silent by contract, so there is no message to read. The work directory holds expected.sha256 and actual.sha256, and checksum-ok.txt is absent
failure_modes.mitigation: read expected.sha256 against actual.sha256 in the work directory: the first is the digest you asserted, the second the digest the file actually has, and they differ. The file is not the artifact the digest names — re-obtain it, and do not clone the copy you have. Do not read the mismatch as a diagnosis of the damage: step 1 cannot tell a corrupted bundle from a truncated one, and does not claim to

failure_modes.symptom: step 2 prints nothing; prerequisites.txt is NOT empty, and bundle-verify.txt names the missing prerequisite commits. history-ok.txt is absent, so step 3 refuses before it clones
failure_modes.mitigation: the bundle is an incremental one; obtain the base repository it was cut against, or a full bundle. Do not read bundle-verify.txt's presence as step 2 having passed: the redirect writes it before git bundle verify has an exit status

failure_modes.symptom: step 2 prints nothing; prerequisites.txt IS empty, bundle-verify.txt carries git's own complaint about the file, and history-ok.txt is absent
failure_modes.mitigation: the file is not a readable bundle — re-obtain it. This is the case the exit status alone cannot tell apart from an incremental bundle, which is why the prerequisite list is parsed

failure_modes.symptom: step 2 succeeds on a bundle whose bytes are damaged or truncated, and step 3 then fails with "error: inflate: data stream error" or "fatal: early EOF", exit 128
failure_modes.mitigation: expected, not a surprise: git bundle verify reads the bundle HEADER and does not inflate the packfile. Damage is caught by the digest when it is honest, and by the clone when it is not — never by step 2. A procedure that stops after git bundle verify is weaker than it reads

failure_modes.symptom: step 2 or step 3 prints nothing and exits non-zero; stderr reads ".../bundle-id.sha256 .../step2-input-id.sha256 differ: byte 1, line 1" (or step3-input-id.sha256). After a step-2 refusal the work directory has no probe/, no prerequisites.txt and no bundle-verify.txt; after a step-3 refusal it has no clone/
failure_modes.mitigation: the BUNDLE_PATH given to that step is not the file step 1 accepted. Read step2-input-id.sha256 or step3-input-id.sha256 against bundle-id.sha256 — the first is what this step was handed, the second what step 1 measured. Give every step the same bundle, or run the other bundle through the whole chain in a fresh work directory. This is the case that used to reach `git clone` and print clone-ok over a foreign repository's bundle, and be caught only by step 4's comparison with the reference tree

failure_modes.symptom: step 2 or step 3 prints nothing and exits 2; stderr reads "cmp: .../bundle-id.sha256: No such file or directory"
failure_modes.mitigation: step 1 has not run in this work directory, or ran and REFUSED: the binding is written past the same check as checksum-ok.txt. Run step 1 first, and past a g1 refusal do not run the chain at all

failure_modes.symptom: step 3 prints nothing and exits non-zero, stderr naming history-ok.txt, even though a step 2 in this same work directory passed earlier — including when step 3 is handed exactly the bundle that step 2 passed
failure_modes.mitigation: not a defect: a later step 2 in the same work directory refused, and step 2 destroys its own token as its first action, so the last step 2 is the only one whose verdict survives. Decide which bundle the work directory is about and run the chain for it from step 1 in a fresh directory. The previous shape of this — the earlier run's token surviving a refusal — let step 3 clone on a verdict that had been overturned, and git then answered on its own terms at exit 128

failure_modes.symptom: a step prints nothing and stderr names a missing artifact of the previous step, e.g. "cat: .../head-commit.txt: No such file or directory" from step 4, "cat: .../checksum-ok.txt: No such file or directory" from step 2, or "cat: .../history-ok.txt: No such file or directory" from step 3
failure_modes.mitigation: run the four steps in order against the same work directory, and give every step the same bundle; each refuses to run without its predecessor's SUCCESS TOKEN and, for steps 2 and 3, without agreeing with step 1's BINDING. Step 2's guard is checksum-ok.txt and step 3's is history-ok.txt, and only a PASSING predecessor writes either. The artifacts they replaced — actual.sha256, written before step 1's check, and bundle-verify.txt, created by the redirect that captures step 2's verify — both survive a refusal, so the presence of either is not permission to continue

failure_modes.symptom: step 4 prints a non-zero count on stdout and exits non-zero; stderr reads "cmp: EOF on .../divergences-expected.txt which is empty", and divergences.txt names the paths
failure_modes.mitigation: either the reference tree carries local edits, or the bundle is not the commit it claims. Read divergences.txt for the paths; the count on stdout says how many. Both signals refuse, so a caller reading either one is safe

evidence.summary: Run against the skillonomia-public release bundle and its extracted reference tree: digest matched, git bundle verify reported a complete history, the clone reproduced HEAD and its tree, and all 171 tracked paths compared equal. The refusals are no longer the author's word: the four defect classes ship in vectors/ with their digests and expected refusals in vectors/MATRIX.tsv, and step 5 has an adopter re-run them on the package in hand — together with three sequence cases, run on the same vectors, that switch the bundle between steps and re-run a step 2 against a stale token. Every step is bound to the artifact step 1 measured, so a token proves this run on this file rather than that some run once passed.
evidence.test_results: positive: g1-digest pass, g2-complete-history pass, g3-clone pass, g4-matches-reference pass, on the release bundle and on vectors/good.bundle. negative, all seven rows of vectors/MATRIX.tsv: corrupt.bundle with the announced digest -> refused at step 1, no clone attempted; corrupt.bundle with its own digest -> steps 1 and 2 pass, refused at step 3, exit 128, inflate data stream error; truncated.bundle with the announced digest -> refused at step 1; truncated.bundle with its own digest -> refused at step 3, early EOF; incremental.bundle -> refused at step 2, prerequisites.txt names the missing commit; foreign.bundle -> steps 1 to 3 pass and step 4 prints divergences 1 and exits non-zero. negative, the three sequence cases, each in its own fresh work directory: g1 good.bundle then g2 foreign.bundle -> g2 exits non-zero, stdout empty, stderr names bundle-id.sha256, and no probe/, prerequisites.txt, bundle-verify.txt or history-ok.txt is created; g1 and g2 good.bundle then g3 foreign.bundle -> g3 exits non-zero, stdout empty, stderr names bundle-id.sha256, no clone/; g1 and g2 good.bundle then g2 incremental.bundle -> the second g2 exits non-zero and history-ok.txt is gone, and g3 then exits non-zero on incremental.bundle AND on good.bundle, naming history-ok.txt and cloning neither. Recorded finding: git bundle verify accepts both the corrupt and the truncated bundle, printing that it records a complete history over a file that cannot clone, so g2 is not a damage check. Second recorded finding, from a live run by an outside operator: a refused g1 used to leave expected.sha256 alone, because actual.sha256 was written on the line after the check and set -e never reached it, while the artifact table promised both — the two step-1 rows now leave the asserted and the measured digest side by side, and the repository's own test executes those rows and reads both files. Third recorded finding, the same defect class one joint further along: step 3 guarded on bundle-verify.txt, which the redirect capturing git bundle verify creates before that command has an exit status. On incremental.bundle offered with its own digest the run went g1 exit 0, g2 exit 1 with bundle-verify.txt present, and step 3 then ran git clone and died at exit 128 on "error: Repository lacks these prerequisite commits" — no bad bundle accepted, but a step running after its predecessor refused, and git's error standing in for a named refusal. Step 2 now writes history-ok.txt past BOTH of its signals and step 3 guards on that: g3 exits non-zero with empty stdout, stderr names history-ok.txt, and no clone directory is created. Fourth and fifth recorded findings, from a live run by an outside operator, and both about what a token does NOT say. (a) A token says a step agreed, not what it agreed ABOUT: in one work directory g1 good.bundle, g2 good.bundle and then g3 on a bundle of an entirely DIFFERENT repository all exited 0, g3 printing head-commit, head-tree, tracked-files and clone-ok over it; step 4 refused with divergences 1, which is a comparison against the reference tree and not the chain holding — a substituted bundle carrying the same tree would have passed that too. Step 1 now writes bundle-id.sha256, the digest it MEASURED past its own check with no path beside it, and steps 2 and 3 each measure their own BUNDLE_PATH and cmp it against that binding before doing anything else: the switch at either joint now exits non-zero with empty stdout, stderr naming the binding, and leaves no probe/, bundle-verify.txt or clone/ behind. (b) A token says a step agreed, not WHEN: g1 good.bundle, g2 good.bundle wrote history-ok.txt, a second g2 on incremental.bundle in the SAME work directory exited non-zero and the first run's token was still there, so g3 ran git clone and died at 128. Step 2 now removes history-ok.txt as its first action and re-writes it only past every signal, so after any refusing step 2 there is no usable token — this run's or the last one's — and step 3 refuses on either bundle, the one the earlier step 2 passed included. Both are executed by the repository's own test, each with its mutant: remove the binding cmp from step 3 and the foreign bundle is cloned and reported clone-ok at exit 0; remove the rm -f from step 2 and step 3 clones on the overturned verdict.

forbidden_actions: modifying the bundle file or the reference tree
running commands from the cloned repository
safety.secrets_policy: The runbook accepts no secrets, reads no credential store and prints only digests, object ids and counts. A bundle is public artifact data; if the repository it carries is not, the work directory inherits that sensitivity and the operator deletes it.
